items.topic: Five items still need design and stories
items.statement: Kobi listed five items that still need design refinement, grooming and user stories: deal lifecycle and CMS sync, commercial terms, VIP workflow, redeposits, and referral payouts (the last two not complete).
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: uh, the five biggest items that are still, uh, that still need design, uh, refinement, grooming, uh, and user stories

items.topic: Deal lifecycle blocks signup logging
items.statement: Kobi said deal lifecycle and CMS sync is the most critical item because it blocks the whole signup logging experience.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: and I'm going to go through the most important mission critical one first, which is the deal, life cycle, and CMS sync. um because that blocks the whole signup logging experience.

items.topic: Simplify new deal creation to core fields
items.statement: To protect the CMS integration, new deal creation will be simplified to core (makeup) fields with gates and controls.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: we need to put a lot of gates and controls around this entire deal creation and management process to make sure that it doesn't break there. What that means is um the new deal creation is going to be far more simplified just core fields.

items.topic: Delete before activation; CMS sync tab
items.statement: A deal can be deleted until it is activated; after activation it syncs to the CMS and cannot be deleted. A new CMS sync tab tracks integration-critical fields (live updating, for admins/ops troubleshooting).
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Once a deal is created um until the deal gets activated um we can still delete the deal. Um once a deal is activated where we can't delete the deal because once a deal is activated that's the indication that it syncs to the CMS. Um there is a new tab called CMS sync which tracks uh few integration critical fields.

items.topic: Makeup editable before activation
items.statement: Until activation the deal is like a draft; editing the makeup updates the IDs and external IDs.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh, but essentially until a deal is activated, I've opened up the ability to edit the makeup uh without it uh like and editing the makeup will update the uh IDs and external IDs on all of that

items.topic: Activation confirmation screen
items.statement: Activation uses a confirmation screen to review the makeup fields required for the CMS integration; after sending, changes need delete-and-recreate or the retire-and-replace process.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. Yeah. There. So, to activate the deal, I put in a confirmation screen so you can do one final review of the makeup fields. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, so these are the required fields uh for the CMS integration, right?

items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Yeah, I think that makes sense. So, why don't we just confirm that you don't need links in order to push it? / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. So, if we sorry, yeah, if we don't need a link, no error.

items.statement: Creating a deal with the same makeup as an existing deal should show an error; Kobi still needs to confirm where that control sits.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: But um if there's a duplicate deal that's created or if we try to create another deal with the same makeup, it should show an error saying there's already an existing deal.

items.statement: Because some Airtable URLs exceed 255 characters (DraftKings, Golden CTM), the link URL uses a long text field; if those URLs are not legitimate, the standard URL field (with built-in validation) could be used instead.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um but looking through your uh air table data um there are quite a few URLs that are over the character limit. So because of that we have to go with the uglier long text field which shows up as like a giant field. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So if this is no longer a case then maybe we just refer to the URL uh field because the URL field also comes with like out of the box validation to make sure that it's an actual URL.

items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I think all of these are draft. Yeah, golden CTM and draft kings are the ones over 255. / Emily Vandenberg: Okay, I will confirm

items.topic: Exclude from CMS toggle on links
items.statement: An 'exclude from CMS' toggle was added on affiliate links (for the VIP workflow) for links that do not sync to the CMS.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. Um, and then the exclude from CMS. Um, we added this as part of the VIP workflow. Um, because there are going to be links that are added that don't necessarily sync to the CMS.

items.topic: Links deactivate only after activation
items.statement: Once a deal is activated and synced, affiliate links cannot be deleted, only deactivated; new links queue a re-sync.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: But once I save this and it's in in the database, we um we won't be able to delete it once the deal is activated and it's synced to C uh CMS. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um but basically uh what what we're doing is once once the deal is synced we can't delete uh the link but you can deactivate it.

items.topic: Sync errors on record plus admin alerts
items.statement: Sync errors show on the deal record, with reports and email notifications to an admin.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. So if there is an error, it is going to show up on the record. Um and the days I will also have reports and email notification set up to also notify an admin so that um we able to catch it right away.

items.topic: Which deal fields lock after activation
items.statement: After activation the makeup fields are locked and non-sync fields stay editable; what can and cannot be deleted is still TBD.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: If you go to edit the deal, all of the makeup fields are locked. Um, anything that's not material to the sync can still be edited. Um, and this is still TBD, so we can finalize uh, what can and cannot be deleted.

items.statement: Per the current API design, a link missing from the payload is treated as deleted, which Kobi called super risky; growing link lists may also exceed payload size limits.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: is if we delete a link here and we send a payload without the link we're going to assume that it's uh it's a link that can be / Kobi Kunasekaran: deleted but I think that's going to be super risky from a integration perspective / Kobi Kunasekaran: we will get to a point where uh the number of or the amount of data that we can send in a single payload for a deal is going to be too big for what the systems are able to accept.

items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh, and notice we we remove the ability to edit the status directly. Um, so we're going to gate it through specific action buttons.

Uh except that you may want to know when signups come in for a pause deal. So we can set up reports slashnotifications if needed to notify you so that you can see what's going on.

items.statement: Joyce explained the CMS batch operator assigns one link to many people; ideally clicking pause in Salesforce turns links off in the CMS automatically. She asked for time to think it through.

That works.

items.statement: Plan: send inactive first, then exclude archived links from later payloads. Needs confirmation with Stra that an omitted link is not deleted, because the current endpoint removes omitted links. Kobi said this is not blocking.

items.topic: Retire as terminal status with replacement
items.statement: Retire is a terminal status: everything locks, the makeup is released, and a replacement deal can be created with a retired/replaces lookup.

You can't do anything else to the deal. Um and you will be able to create a replacement deal.

notes: Transcript runs about 3h26m (00:00:01-03:26:36), mostly a prototype design walkthrough: deal lifecycle/CMS sync, commercial terms, VIP signup flow, redeposits/budgets, referral payouts. No Jira keys were spoken. In-meeting changes: (1) parent-container deal versioning discussed, then a single deal record suggested (still somewhat open); (2) 'return allocation' became 'request reallocation' with mandatory notes; (3) budget -> budget entry -> allocation model reduced to monthly budget -> allocation; (4) eligible-signup dates moved from budget config to the allocation record with a deal-level default. Gemini 'Next steps' lists 'Lena' to review; the invite shows lina@wagertech.bet (ASR/spelling). One passage about a team member's time off was not recorded (rule 5). Summary 'yes' marks mean the Gemini section matches in substance; 'no' items are listed in gemini_disagreements.
